claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You're asking about your son Alex who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, sixth form, or undertaking approved training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Alex studying for his A-levels at college would count as approved education.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex and his living situation:

**Do you live with Alex, or if he lives elsewhere, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do contribute towards his upkeep - I help with clothes, books for college, and some of his living expenses. I give about £26 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know you're contributing towards Alex's upkeep.

To complete my assessment, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, the other parent or someone else he may be living with?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits himself.

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Alex qualifies** - Even though he's 18, Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 who are in approved education or training, and his A-level studies at college count as approved education.

✓ **You meet the responsibility requirement** - Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing approximately £26 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, books, and living expenses), which meets the requirement of supporting him financially.

✓ **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement.

✓ **No conflicts** - Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

✓ **Alex's circumstances** - He's not working 24+ hours per week and is not claiming benefits in his own right, both of which could have affected eligibility.

**Important note:** Please be aware of the High Income Child Benefit tax charge - if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay a tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator on GOV.UK to check this.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through GOV.UK. If you have any questions about making a claim, feel free to ask!
